solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Showing nobility, pounds replaced by pair at financial risk

indicators.note: says the pounds letter is swapped out and the pair abbreviation takes its place

parts.note: sublime means noble, exalted in character
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: A nobleman whose fortune has been swapped for a pair of something is now financially exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: SUBLIME with its L (pounds) replaced by PR (pair) gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Subprime loans go to borrowers with poor credit, so they carry a high risk of default.

clue.text: Discerning in saint a goodness, right away

indicators.note: says the right letter goes away from the exclamation

parts.note: goodness gracious, so gracious is an exclamation like goodness

explanation.surface: Spotting the goodness in a saint shows good judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goodness' looks like a noun, but it is the exclamation 'Gracious!'; GRACIOUS without R gives GACIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagacious means wise and shrewd, showing keen judgement.

clue.text: Unusual attire bishop's put on? Yes and no

definitions.text: Unusual attire bishop's put on? Yes and no

indicators.note: in a down clue, put on places the bishop letter above the rest

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of attire appear in an odd arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Is this odd outfit something a bishop wears? Sort of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no' admits the whole clue is only half true: a biretta is clerical wear, but hardly unusual for a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the square cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy, so it is attire a bishop puts on.

clue.text: Passenger maybe arresting a looter

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the passenger word holds the letter

parts.note: a passenger is an example of a rider

explanation.surface: A passenger turns out to be holding a looter.
explanation.walkthrough: RIDER holds A.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider is someone who attacks to plunder, a looter.

clue.text: He entrances me, surviving at first in southern desert

indicators.note: the first letter sits inside the desert word

parts.note: desert means merit, as in getting one's just deserts

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of surviving

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A desert survivor is mesmerised by a figure in the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like sand, but it is what one deserves, as in just deserts.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesmerist is a hypnotist, one who puts people into a trance.

clue.text: Girl presented a note for discussion

parts.note: a deb (debutante) is a girl presented at court or in society
TE is a note of the sol-fa scale, also spelt ti

explanation.surface: A girl offers up a written note to start a conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: A debutante is formally presented to society, so 'Girl presented' together gives DEB.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is a formal discussion in which opposing arguments are put.

clue.text: Boxer's in mire over philosophical principle

indicators.note: the boxer's letters go inside the reversed mud
in a down clue, over turns the mire word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: mire is mud
Muhammad Ali was the boxer, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A boxer stuck in the mud ponders his philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: Muhammad Ali is the crossword's default boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dualism is the doctrine that reality has two fundamental kinds, such as mind and matter.

clue.text: For work meetings at home, at first get into underclothes

indicators.note: into says the home and get letters are slipped inside the underclothes word

parts.note: briefs are underpants
in means at home

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of get

explanation.surface: Advice for home working: put on underwear before the video call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For work meetings' reads as the purpose of dressing, but it is the definition; IN and G go into BRIEFS.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefings are meetings at work where staff are given information or instructions.

clue.text: Vestment in large container left in reserve

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for wine or beer

indicators.note: the left letter goes in the reserve word

parts.note: ice means reserve, coolness of manner

explanation.surface: A church garment kept in a big storage box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' is not a store but cool aloofness: ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunicle is a short liturgical tunic worn by a subdeacon or bishop, a church vestment.

clue.text: Fish, confused, bled out

indicators.note: tells us the word bled is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: garbled means confused or jumbled
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fish, muddled and drained of blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' looks like an anagram signal, but it is GARBLED; take BLED out and three letters remain.
explanation.definitionFit: The gar is a long, slender fish with a beak-like snout full of teeth.

clue.text: Exposure to sun in quarantine, around noon

indicators.note: the quarantine word goes round the noon letter

parts.note: quarantine is a period of isolation

explanation.surface: Someone in quarantine catches the midday sun.
explanation.walkthrough: N (noon) goes inside ISOLATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolation is the technical term for being exposed to the sun's rays, or the solar radiation received.

clue.text: Accountant set out agreement for gems

parts.note: CA is a Chartered Accountant

indicators.note: set out suggests the letters are laid out afresh in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
yes is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: An accountant draws up a contract dealing in precious stones.
explanation.walkthrough: CA, then the letters of SET rearranged as TSE, then YES.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat's-eyes are gemstones such as chrysoberyl showing a narrow band of reflected light, like a cat's pupil.

clue.text: How posh people used to pronounce actually spread disease

indicators.text: How posh people used to pronounce
indicators.note: the old cut-glass upper-class accent turned the short a of fact into a short e

parts.note: in fact means actually

explanation.surface: A remark about how the upper classes really did spread germs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fact' in the clipped vowels of old upper-class English speech, such as the Queen's early broadcasts, comes out as 'in fect'.
explanation.definitionFit: To infect is to pass on a disease to someone, spreading it.

clue.text: Embargo applied to old port

indicators.note: the embargo is applied to, placed after, the old letter

parts.note: an embargo is a ban on trade

explanation.surface: An old harbour has a trade embargo slapped on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Oban is a ferry port on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a Scottish harbour town, gateway to the Hebrides, so it is an example of a port.

clue.text: Opera and musical in back-to-back clash, setting a standard

indicators.note: the two titles collide, sharing their A so one copy goes

parts.note: Norma is the opera by Bellini

indicators.note: the musical faces the opposite way, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: An opera and a musical scheduled against each other.
explanation.walkthrough: NORMA is followed by EVITA backwards (ATIVE); the two A's collide into one.
explanation.definitionFit: Normative means establishing a norm, prescribing how things should be.

clue.text: Principled school looked after children?

parts.note: a high is a high school
a childminder minds children, so minded is looked after them

explanation.surface: A school that cared for its pupils is called upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone high-minded has lofty moral standards, so is principled.

clue.text: One providing simple treatment as dog run over in robbery

indicators.note: the reversed letters go in the robbery word

parts.note: a heist is a robbery

indicators.note: in a down clue, over flips the dog and run letters to read backwards

parts.note: lab is a Labrador dog
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A dog gets run over during a robbery, needing first aid.
explanation.walkthrough: A simple is an old word for a medicinal herb, which is why 'simple treatment' points to plant remedies.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbalist supplies remedies made from plants, once called simples.

clue.text: Party till early hours, in which I see texting double

parts.note: the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party

indicators.note: the texting letters go in the late word

parts.note: staying up late means till the early hours
IC is how I see is written in a text message

explanation.surface: Someone partying till dawn sees their texts arriving twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' is not a do but the DUP, Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A duplicate is an exact copy, a double of something.

clue.text: A little yarn to line clothes for the summer ahead

indicators.note: says the summer clothes come in front of the rest

parts.note: shorts are worn in summer
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A tip for lining your summer wardrobe, or a short knitting instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' looks like knitting wool, but here it is a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarn is informal for a tale, so a brief tale of fiction fits the literary form.

clue.text: Responsible youth's pressure upset lout

parts.note: a head of steam is a build-up of pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the lout word upside down

parts.note: a yob is a lout

explanation.surface: A responsible youngster is upset by a lout's pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: A head boy is the senior pupil chosen to represent a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: The head boy is a senior pupil given responsibility for leading and representing the school.

clue.text: Pistol not used at the front?

definitions.text: Pistol not used at the front?

parts.words: Pistol not used at the front?
parts.note: a weapon worn at one's flank, and read another way an arm carried at the side rather than the front

explanation.walkthrough: 'The front' suggests the battlefront; the joke is that this pistol sits at the hip, not the front of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidearm is a small weapon such as a pistol worn in a holster at the hip.

clue.text: Very cheerful, but in trouble here?

definitions.note: the idiom 'in the soup' means in trouble, so this is where you are when in trouble

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
up means in good spirits

explanation.surface: A puzzle: how can someone be so happy while in difficulties?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: being 'in the soup' is a British idiom for being in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom being in the soup means being in a mess, so this is the place where trouble lies.

clue.text: Nothing difficult about raising crops in the front garden

indicators.note: the nothing and difficult letters go about, round, the picked letters

parts.note: O is the zero digit, nothing
hard means difficult

indicators.note: takes the front letter of each of the words raising and crops

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Growing crops in a front garden isn't hard at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front garden' looks like a phrase, but 'in the front' takes R and C, which O HARD goes about.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a garden or enclosure of fruit trees.

clue.text: American organisation holds people up in darkened room

indicators.note: the American organisation's letters hold the reversed people

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

indicators.note: in a down clue, up reads the people word upward, backwards

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: US intelligence detains people in a dark room.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN read upward is NEM, held in CIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinema is an auditorium kept dark so films can be projected.

clue.text: Joker put round a new rumour

indicators.note: the joker word is placed around the other letters

parts.note: a card is a joker, a wag

explanation.surface: A prankster spreads a fresh piece of gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: A and N (new) go inside CARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is an unfounded story or false report, a rumour.

clue.text: Girl "I just met" with Greek character making music in Mexico

parts.note: the West Side Story song Maria begins 'I just met a girl named Maria'
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a girl they just met and a Greek, playing Mexican music.
explanation.definitionFit: Mariachi is the traditional Mexican folk music played by strolling bands with trumpets and guitars.

clue.text: Through seawater ploughed giant ship

indicators.note: the reworked giant passes through the seawater word, sitting inside it

parts.note: brine is salt water, the sea

indicators.note: ploughed means churned up, so the letters of giant are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A giant ship ploughs through the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Through' reads as motion across the sea, but it puts the reworked letters inside the seawater word.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel, a kind of ship.

clue.text: A hard answer I suddenly see

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils; the answer also runs across 'A hard', which is coincidence

explanation.surface: A solver's moment of realisation on a tough question.
explanation.definitionFit: Aha is the exclamation of sudden understanding or recognition.

clue.text: My clue confused lecture hall

indicators.note: confused means muddled up, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter admits a clue baffled a lecture room.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyceum is a hall for public lectures, after Aristotle's school in Athens.

clue.text: Separate legs, taking seat across sides of tractor

indicators.note: the seat word lies across, around, the letters from the tractor

parts.note: a saddle is a seat on a horse or bike

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmer sits astride a tractor seat, legs apart.
explanation.walkthrough: SADDLE goes across TR, the first and last letters of tractor.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle is to sit or stand with the legs wide apart, either side of something.
